fullPassage: Baarle is a small border village where areas of Belgian land are scattered within the surrounding Dutch territory. To make things more confusing, there are some Belgian areas within the Dutch territory that contain smaller Dutch properties. It is one of only a few places in the world that have such a complicated border. In 1995, the Belgian and Dutch governments decided to clearly mark the unusual border with a line on the ground. If the border line runs through the middle of buildings such as houses and cafes, it cuts them in half, and each part belongs to a different country. Which country do you live in if your house is divided by this line? This is determined by where your front door is! So if the Dutch annoyed you last week, all you have to do is move your front door to relocate to Belgium.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: confuse(동사: 혼란시키다) → confusing(형용사: 혼란스러운). make + 목적어 + 형용사 보어 구문
det.analysis: confuse를 형용사 confusing으로 변환. 'To make things more confusing' = '상황을 더 혼란스럽게 만들다' — make + 목적어(things) + 형용사(confusing) 구조에서 형용사가 필요
det.tip: make things more _____ → 형용사 자리 → confusing

questions.passage: Which country do you live in if your house is divided by this line? This is __________ (determine) by where your front door is!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: determine(동사: 결정하다) → determined(과거분사: 결정되는). 수동태 be determined 구문
det.analysis: determine을 과거분사 determined로 변환. 'This is determined by' = '이것은 ~에 의해 결정된다' — be + p.p. 수동태 구문에서 과거분사가 필요
det.tip: This is _____ by ~ → 수동태(be + p.p.) → determined

questions.passage: Baarle is a small border village where areas of Belgian land are scattered within the surrounding Dutch territory. To make things more confusing, there are some Belgian areas within the Dutch territory that contain smaller Dutch properties. It is one of only a few places in the world that have such a complicated border. In 1995, the Belgian and Dutch governments decided to clearly mark the unusual border with a line __________. If the border line runs through the middle of buildings such as houses and cafes, it cuts them in half, and each part belongs to a different country. Which country do you live in if your house is divided by this line? This is determined by where your front door is! So if the Dutch annoyed you last week, all you have to do is move your front door to relocate to Belgium.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: on the ground=땅 위에 / in the air=공중에 / under the sea=바다 밑에 / on the wall=벽에
det.analysis:
① on the ground: 국경을 땅 위에 선으로 표시했다 ←정답
② in the air: 공중에 선을? 문맥 부적절
③ under the sea: 바다 밑에? 문맥 부적절
④ on the wall: 벽에? 국경 표시 문맥 부적절
det.tip: mark the border with a line ___ → 땅 위에(on the ground) 선을 그음

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: in advance=미리 / in half=반으로 / at once=즉시 / by chance=우연히
det.analysis:
① in advance: 미리? 문맥 부적절
② in half: 국경선이 건물을 반으로 자르고, 각 부분이 서로 다른 나라에 속함 ←정답
③ at once: 즉시? 문맥 부적절
④ by chance: 우연히? 문맥 부적절
det.tip: cuts them ___ + each part belongs to a different country → 반으로(in half)
